assumptions.name: beta
assumptions.justification: Regressed against S&P 500 on monthly total returns to 2026-09-11, over 72 paired observations. The proxy and the window are both judgements and both change the answer, which is why this is a proposal rather than an input.

assumptions.name: depreciation_intensity
assumptions.justification: The mean of depreciation and amortisation over revenue across 5 period(s) ending 2021-12-31, 2022-12-31, 2023-12-31, 2024-12-31, 2025-12-31. The individual observations were 0.1745, 0.1236, 0.1017, 0.0873, 0.0866.

assumptions.name: ebit_margin
assumptions.justification: The mean of operating income over revenue across 5 period(s) ending 2021-12-31, 2022-12-31, 2023-12-31, 2024-12-31, 2025-12-31. The individual observations were 0.0282, 0.0847, 0.1788, 0.1850, 0.2340.

assumptions.name: exit_multiple
assumptions.justification: Large-cap pharma in a mature, capital-intensive, regulated industry with recurring patent cliffs — that argues for a multiple near the middle of the 2x-40x band rather than the software end. EV/EBITDA rather than EV/EBIT matters here because the derived D&A intensity is high relative to the derived EBIT margin (acquired-intangible amortisation, Alexion), so EBITDA flatters operating economics; I have discounted for that. Note plainly: I have no stored peer-multiple fact to point at, so this leans on convention and should be checked against current peer EV/EBITDA before use. Consistency: 11x and 2.5% describe the same mature, modestly-growing business. Of the two, I regard the perpetual growth rate as the better terminal-value estimate, because a multiple imported from today's market embeds current sentiment about pipelines that will have turned over entirely by the terminal year.

assumptions.name: revenue_growth
assumptions.justification: The compound annual growth rate of revenue from 2021-12-31 to 2025-12-31, over 4 year(s): revenue moved from 37,417,000,000 to 58,739,000,000. Held flat across the forecast, because a trailing rate is one number and projecting a fade is a judgement this derivation does not make.

assumptions.name: terminal_growth
assumptions.justification: Taken to be below a cost of capital of at least 7% for a large, investment-grade, USD-funded pharma; it clears any ordinary WACC with room. Rests on: a globally diversified five-therapy-area portfolio in categories (oncology, rare disease, metabolic) growing faster than GDP, offset in perpetuity by the patent-cliff pattern the research documents directly (Brilinta -33%, Soliris -30% CER) and by US pricing policy now acting structurally on price (the October 2025 pricing agreement, Section 232). Net: modest real growth plus inflation, not the 11.9% trailing CAGR. Lower it toward 0.02 if pipeline replacement is judged weaker or US price cuts permanent; raise toward 0.03 only on a view that pharma pricing power outpaces nominal GDP for ever.

assumptions.name: working_capital_intensity
assumptions.justification: The mean of net working capital — current assets less current liabilities — over revenue, across 5 period(s) ending 2021-12-31, 2022-12-31, 2023-12-31, 2024-12-31, 2025-12-31. A negative figure is normal for a business paid before it pays, and is proposed as it stands rather than floored at zero.
